title: Reentrant Universal Exception Logging Panic (Log Storm)
pattern: An exception or error handler that attempts to write error information to a local disk or database, and upon catching an error inside the logging utility itself, recursively calls the logging function or spawns a thread to log it.
why_bad: If the local filesystem becomes full (ENOSPC), standard write calls will consistently fail [608]. A reentrant logger that handles writing failures by immediately attempting to log the failure will enter an infinite recursion loop [217]. This causes CPU utilization to spike to 100% and rapidly consumes stack space or heap memory, triggering an immediate crash [217].
detection: Identify error handlers that attempt I/O logging operations where the failure path (recovery/fallback block) invokes the same logging API.
fix: Error handlers must be simple and robust. Logging failures should fall back to non-blocking memory buffers or direct `stderr` writing without recursive path execution [217, 608].
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 10 (Steady State) / passages [217, 608].
